summary: All round 2 findings are closed or accepted. C2-F1 is closed: the focus rule at look.css:44-48 now uses :is(a, button, [tabindex]):focus-visible with specificity (0,2,0) for the outline and an !important 6 px brown box-shadow, so no control rule can hide the ring. Gate row 19 reads the computed ring on a decodable word button, a mode button, a week tile link, and the sign-in button, and all four show the brown 6 px shadow and the 3 px white outline. C2-F2 is closed: every plaque rule (base, band, landscape) fits the font from var(--title-chars), with its own floor and cap. C2-F4 is closed: the comment now says 7.09:1 and 4.92:1. C2-F3 stays a nit that the orchestrator accepted. No route, label, href, form, or API response changed in the r4 range (only done-mark.tsx, a comment line). The captures show the logo, the label, the plaque, the tiles, and the highlight with no overlap. No new blocking defect.
nonblocking_findings: C2-F3 [Nit] review-c: A 60-character title at 844 x 390 can still touch the level and week label. look.css:783-786 fits the font to the 20 px floor, and the title wraps to two lines. The plaque then spans about y 30 to 80 and the label spans y 18 to 41 at x 72 to about 232. The overlap is the same stress case as in round 2. No shipped title (6 to 13 characters) reaches it. The orchestrator accepted this as a nit; I keep it listed and do not escalate it. Proposal: ACCEPT.

C3-F1 [Nit] review-c: The broad selector [tabindex] in look.css:44 also matches the read-along sentence (tabIndex 0) and the word (tabIndex -1) from read-along-passage.tsx:111 and :170. The !important brown shadow replaces the Tailwind ring and offset on those elements. The result is still a two-tone ring (white 3 px outline, brown 6 px), so the user sees a ring, and the 6 px shadow can touch a neighbor word. No gate row focuses a read-along word. Proposal: ACCEPT, or add one gate row for a focused read-along word in Phase 3.
